deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): a von Neumann algebra (or C*-algebra) with a faithful, normal, semi-finite trace T. The underlined letters are ideals attached to T:
- \underline{a}: the ideal of definition of T, i.e. the span of positive elements of finite trace.
- \underline{b}: probably the larger ideal of 'T-compact' elements, those whose spectral projections away from 0 have finite trace.
- \underline{c}: the algebra on which the commutative reduction is done.
The previous page shows the commutative case. A commutative piece is identified with C_0(M), and the trace restricted to it is a Radon measure: T(f) = ∫ f dμ.

Corollary 2. If A ∈ \underline{b} is normal and f is Borel on C, bounded on compacts and zero near 0, then f(A) ∈ \underline{a}. The reason is that f(A) = f(A)E_ε, where E_ε is the spectral projection of |A| ≥ ε, which has finite trace.

Spectral measure. For normal A, put A in a maximal commutative subalgebra ≅ C(M). Define the measure μ_A on C* = C\{0} by
(1) ⟨φ, μ_A⟩ = T(φ(A)) for φ ∈ K(C*) (continuous, compact support in C*).
This is the image of the trace measure under the Gelfand transform of A. It does not depend on the choice of commutative subalgebra.
Properties stated:
- support μ_A = σ(A) (off 0);
- formula (1) extends to φ integrable;
- A ∈ \underline{a} ⇔ ∫|z| dμ_A < ∞ (presumably what is meant);
- moments (3): ∫ z^n dμ_A = T(A^n) for n ≥ 1.

Positive case, A ≥ 0. The 'fonction spectrale décroissante' φ_A on R^+_* is the decreasing rearrangement of A relative to T: φ_A(s) = inf{λ : T(E_{(λ,∞)}(A)) ≤ s}. It is decreasing and φ_A(0+) = ‖A‖. Define (4):
- Φ_A(t) = ∫_0^t φ_A (Ky Fan-type norms);
- Ψ_A(t) = ∫_0^t log φ_A;
- Δ_A(t) = exp Ψ_A(t), a truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant.
The next page sets Δ_A = Δ_{|A|} for general A. When ω = T(1) < ∞ it recovers Δ(A) = Δ_A(ω), the Fuglede–Kadison determinant.

Purpose: this is a draft of the machinery of Grothendieck's Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'. The aim is to transfer Weyl/Ky Fan/Hardy–Littlewood majorization inequalities and the determinant to semi-finite traces.
errors: 'support μ_A = σ(A)' can only hold away from 0. μ_A lives on C*, so the correct statement is supp μ_A = closure of (σ(A)\{0}), or σ(A)∪{0} in the non-unital/infinite-trace case.
φ_A(0) = ‖A‖ needs the right-continuous convention for the rearrangement (φ_A(0+) = ‖A‖).

The moment formula ∫ z^n dμ_A = T(A^n) requires A ∈ \underline{a} (trace class relative to T), at least for n = 1. Higher n are fine if A ∈ \underline{b} ∩ L^n. The page leaves this hypothesis implicit.
μ_A is only a Radon measure on C* (it may be infinite near 0). Independence from the chosen maximal abelian subalgebra is asserted, not proved.

ideas.what: Functions of a T-compact normal operator vanishing near 0 lie in the definition ideal of the trace
ideas.where_published: probably implicit in Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955)

ideas.what: Spectral distribution measure of a normal operator relative to a trace, with moments T(A^n)
ideas.modern_name: distribution (spectral measure) of a normal element in a tracial W*-probability space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Murray–von Neumann / Segal; standard in free probability

ideas.what: Decreasing rearrangement φ_A of a positive operator relative to a semi-finite trace
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fack–Kosaki 1986 (also Ovchinnikov 1970); Grothendieck 1955 is the original

ideas.what: Φ_A(t) = ∫_0^t φ_A, Ky Fan-type functionals for majorization
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan norms / Hardy–Littlewood majorization in semifinite algebras

ideas.what: Δ_A(t) = exp ∫_0^t log φ_{|A|}, a truncated determinant, giving the Fuglede–Kadison determinant at t = T(1)
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant; logarithmic submajorization (Weyl-type) in semifinite algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fuglede–Kadison 1952; Weyl inequality extensions by Fack (1982), Fack–Kosaki, Haagerup–Schultz
ideas.where_published: Possibly Bourbaki exp. 113 (it treats convexity inequalities and determinants); not verified

missed.claim: Archival draft showing Grothendieck already in 1953 had the generalized s-numbers and a t-truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant for semi-finite traces. The literature mostly credits the s-numbers to Fack–Kosaki (1986). This page documents priority and the route: commutative reduction via C_0(M) plus the trace measure.
missed.quote: Ψ_A(t) = ∫_0^t log φ_A(s) ds ; Δ_A = Δ_f = exp Ψ_f
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only. The mathematics is now standard (Fack–Kosaki, Haagerup–Schultz determinant/Brown-measure work). The determinant function Δ_A(t) for infinite traces is a mild anticipation of later semifinite determinant theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material that became Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955). The ideas (spectral measure relative to a trace, decreasing rearrangement, Ky Fan functionals, truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant) are known and largely published, though often credited to later authors. The only novelty is historical documentation of the 1953 date and of the t-dependent determinant.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'bornée sur les compacts' (the struck word is illegible).
'K(C^*)' is the space of continuous compactly supported functions on C* = C\{0}.
The boxed formula reads 'support μ_A = σ(A)' with the gloss '(spectre de A)'.
The rearrangement line should read: 'c'est une fonction décroissante sur R^+_*, φ_A(0) = ‖A‖'. The quotation marks in the transcription stand for φ_A(0).
The garbled phrase about A ∈ \underline{a} is presumably 'A ∈ \underline{a} ⟺ |z| est μ_A-intégrable'.
Last line: 'Δ_A = Δ_f = exp Ψ_f'; the struck alternative is Δ_A(t) = exp ∫_0^t log φ_A(s) ds.
